newsitem.title: UK: Camelot shareholders angry over non-profit plans.
newsitem.headline: Camelot shareholders angry over non-profit plans.

text.p: Main shareholders in UK national lottery operator Camelot have expressed concern over proposals to run the lottery as a non-profit organisation, UK newspaper reports said.

Racal Electronics Plc and De La Rue Plc, which each own 22.5 percent of Camelot, and U.S. shareholder GTECH expressed their misgivings over being a part of a non-profit organisation running the lottery.
Racal chairman Ernest Harrison said Racal could withdraw from Camelot if the lottery became a non-profit organisation and De La Rue refused to rule out a similar move, said the Times newspaper.

Of the other two shareholders, ICL, the British-based computer company owned by Fujitsu Ltd, said it was awaiting the government's proposals while Cadbury Schweppes declined to comment, according to the Financial Times newspaper.

Sir George Russell, chairman of Camelot, said on Monday he had agreed with the government to explore ways of turning the lottery into a not-for-profit organisation. National Heritage Secretary Chris Smith summoned Russell on Monday to express the government's outrage that Camelot's executive salary bill rose 40 percent in the year to March while the sums it raised for good causes fell.
